alert.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued September 14 at 2:46AM CDT until September 15 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI

alerts.headline: Small Craft Advisory issued September 14 at 2:46AM CDT until September 15 at 7:00PM CDT by NWS Green Bay WI
alerts.description:
* WHAT...For the first Small Craft Advisory, south winds 15 to
20 kt with gusts up to 30 kt and waves 3 to 6 ft expected. For
the Gale Warning, south winds 20 to 25 kt with gusts up to 40
kt and waves 6 to 12 ft expected. For the second Small Craft
Advisory, southwest winds 10 to 20 kt veering west, with gusts
up to 30 kt and waves 7 to 10 ft expected.

* WHERE...Lake Michigan nearshore waters from Washington Island
to Sheboygan.

* WHEN...For the first Small Craft Advisory, from 4 PM this
afternoon to 9 PM CDT this evening. For the Gale Warning, from
9 PM this evening to 7 AM CDT Tuesday. For the second Small
Craft Advisory, from 7 AM to 7 PM CDT Tuesday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous waves which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.

headline.wave_station_label: Rawley Point East buoy (NDBC 45210) — open lake, deep water

explain.text: Wind has come mostly from the south and west-northwest over the past 3 days. Under PierBite's wind model, wind from that quarter can pull colder water in toward the shore.

Wind favoured cold water for most of the past 3 days, but it has swung back onshore in the last 12 hours. Under PierBite's wind model, a recent shift like that can push cold water away from the pier before it arrives, so the score is held down.

headline.wind_station_label: Sheboygan County Memorial Airport (nearest continuously-reporting wind station)

explain.text: Wind has come mostly from the south and northwest over the past 3 days. Under PierBite's wind model, wind from that quarter can pull colder water in toward the shore.

headline.wind_station_label: Kewaunee MET station (nearest continuously-reporting wind station)

explain.text: Wind has come mostly from the south and northwest over the past 3 days. Under PierBite's wind model, wind from that quarter can pull colder water in toward the shore. This pier has no wind sensor of its own, so the reading comes from Kewaunee.

headline.wind_station_label: Kewaunee MET station (nearest continuously-reporting wind station)

explain.text: Wind favoured cold water for most of the past 3 days, but it has swung back onshore in the last 12 hours. Under PierBite's wind model, a recent shift like that can push cold water away from the pier before it arrives, so the score is held down.

open_lake_context.buoy_label: Rawley Point East buoy (NDBC 45210) — open lake, deep water
open_lake_context.note: Open-lake and nearshore water are not the same water. This is the difference between a reading taken at the pier and one taken in deep water offshore.
